answer: A network can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to custody a unique encrypted shard of the shared nebula archive: on joining, an agent receives a random shard and must re-prove possession each epoch. A sparrow-light client stores only one shard, so honest cost stays tiny, but a farmer running a thousand puppets must store a thousand distinct shards and answer a thousand unpredictable retrieval challenges, each sealed with a fresh cipher that cannot be precomputed or shared. Storage and bandwidth then scale linearly with fake identities, while honest agents pay once.
